subject: science
passage: Monarch butterfly caterpillars feed on milkweed and store the plant's toxic chemicals in their bodies, so adult monarchs taste bitter and often make birds that eat them vomit. Birds that have had this experience tend to avoid orange-and-black butterflies afterward. The viceroy butterfly, which looks very similar to the monarch, was long assumed to be harmless to eat, although later tests showed that viceroys can also taste unpleasant to birds. Whether or not a viceroy itself tastes bad, its resemblance to the monarch likely means that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: birds are more likely to attack viceroys than to attack monarchs.
choices.B: viceroys are the only butterflies that birds have learned to avoid.
choices.C: birds that avoid monarchs are also likely to avoid viceroys.
choices.D: viceroy caterpillars must feed on milkweed in order to survive.

explanation.why: Birds sickened by monarchs learn to avoid orange-and-black butterflies, and viceroys look very much like monarchs. Regardless of their own taste, viceroys therefore probably benefit when birds avoid them by mistaking them for monarchs.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Looking like a monarch would make birds less likely, not more likely, to attack a viceroy.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Birds avoid monarchs too, and the text gives no basis for saying viceroys are the only ones avoided.
explanation.C: Correct. A bird that avoids orange-and-black butterflies would likely avoid the look-alike viceroy as well.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says monarch caterpillars eat milkweed; it never says what viceroy caterpillars eat.
